title: The student pilot toolkit: say again, slower

briefing.description: Every student's secret weapons: the phrase “student pilot” (controllers will slow down and simplify — it's in the AIM), “radio check”, and “say again slower”. In this scenario the Ground controller talks fast and you will NOT catch it all. That's the point. Asking for a repeat is professional; guessing on a readback is not.
briefing.atisText: Centerville Regional information {atis}. Wind {wind_dir} at {wind_kt}. Visibility one zero. Sky clear. Altimeter {altimeter}. Landing and departing runway {rwy}. Advise on initial contact you have information {atis}.

steps.speaker: ATIS
steps.text: Centerville Regional information {atis}. Wind {wind_dir} at {wind_kt}. Visibility one zero. Sky clear. Altimeter {altimeter}. Landing and departing runway {rwy}. Advise on initial contact you have information {atis}.
The radios just came back from the avionics shop, and this is your first solo trip to a towered field. Before asking for taxi, confirm the radio actually works.

steps.prompt: Ask Ground for a radio check, and let them know you're a student pilot.
steps.hint: Centerville Ground, Skyhawk {callsign}, student pilot, radio check.

elements.label: the “student pilot” callout
elements.feedbackMissing: Say “student pilot” — the AIM recommends it, and controllers genuinely slow down for you.

steps.speaker: Ground
steps.text: Skyhawk {callsign}, Centerville Ground, loud and clear.
Radio confirmed. Now ask for taxi — you're at the main ramp with information {atis}.

steps.prompt: Request taxi for pattern work: who you are, where you are, the ATIS.
steps.hint: Centerville Ground, Skyhawk {callsign}, student pilot, at the main ramp with information {atis}, ready to taxi for pattern work.

elements.label: your position on the field
elements.feedbackMissing: Tell Ground where you are: “at the main ramp”.

elements.label: the ATIS code
elements.feedbackWrong: You said information {heard}, but the current ATIS is {atis}.

steps.speaker: Ground
steps.text: Skyhawk {callsign} Centerville Ground runway {rwy} taxi via alpha cross runway two two hold short of runway {rwy} at alpha three traffic is a King Air taxiing opposite direction.
…That was a firehose. You caught “runway {rwy}” and “via alpha” — the rest blurred past. Do NOT guess on a readback. Ask.

steps.prompt: Ask Ground to say it again, slower.
steps.hint: Skyhawk {callsign}, student pilot, say again slower please.

elements.label: the say-again request
elements.feedbackMissing: Just ask: “say again slower”. Controllers vastly prefer a repeat over a wrong readback.

elements.label: your callsign
elements.feedbackMissing: Include your callsign so Ground knows who's asking.

steps.speaker: Ground
steps.text: Skyhawk {callsign}, no problem. Runway {rwy}... taxi via alpha... cross runway two two... then hold short of runway {rwy}.

steps.prompt: Now you have all of it. Read back every piece: runway, route, the crossing, and the hold short.
steps.hint: Runway {rwy}, taxi via alpha, cross runway two two, hold short runway {rwy}, Skyhawk {callsign}.

elements.label: runway readback
elements.feedbackWrong: You read back runway {heard}, but Ground assigned runway {rwy}.

elements.label: runway crossing readback
elements.feedbackMissing: Read back the crossing: “cross runway two two” — runway crossings always get read back.

elements.label: hold-short readback
elements.feedbackMissing: Read back the hold short — word for word, every time.

steps.speaker: Ground
steps.text: Skyhawk {callsign}, readback correct. Nicely done — and don't hesitate to ask again, that's what we're here for.
Lesson locked in: “student pilot”, “radio check”, and “say again slower” are tools, not confessions. The pros use them too.
